key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and identify high-efficiency, lead-free architectures with clear materials-level design rules.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical screening strategy for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations to accelerate development of scalable, environmentally friendly perovskite solar cells.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device architectures in SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong ranking performance, and the best verified devices reached 28.85% PCE for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag and 28.62% for FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness of the training subset and the assumptions of SCAPS-1D, so predictions should be validated before experimental deployment.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
